bibliographic.title: Governing Patient-Facing AI-Generated Video in Digital Health: A Risk-and-Ethics Matrix for Deployment, Monitoring, and Change Control
bibliographic.citation_apa: Hu, Y., & Jiang, W. (2026). Governing patient-facing AI-generated video in digital health: A risk-and-ethics matrix for deployment, monitoring, and change control. Journal of Medical Internet Research, 28, e91940. https://doi.org/10.2196/91940

methodology.method_family: viewpoint with literature synthesis and theoretical framework development
methodology.study_design: Viewpoint proposing a risk-and-ethics matrix framework
methodology.technology_context: patient-facing high-fidelity AI-generated video (synthetic or substantially AI-mediated video with realistic human likeness, voices, or clinical communication cues); text-to-video explainers; clinician avatars; deepfake-style media in patient portals, telehealth, apps, and social platforms

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed JMIR Viewpoint that proposes an operational, life-cycle governance framework for patient-facing generative AI video in health care, with strong relevance to risk management, ethics, monitoring, human-in-the-loop review, and change control. It does not primarily address conversational LLM systems, chatbots, agents, or RAG; generative AI video governance is the central object, so it is better classified as foundational/contextual rather than central conversational-LLM evidence.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Verify whether brief mentions of chatbots and ChatGPT (manuscript editing only) justify any upgrade to supporting_evidence for conversational governance themes; confirm absence of primary focus on LLM-based dialogue systems.

appraisal.notes: Appropriate as a conceptual Viewpoint with literature synthesis; no empirical sample or systematic review methods are described in the provided text. Framework presentation is clear, but evidentiary basis for matrix thresholds and disposition rules appears primarily argumentative and integrative rather than empirically validated.

cerqual.explanation: The framework is internally coherent and explicitly links governance dispositions to controls and monitoring, but the provided text shows no primary data collection or validation study. Relevance to the review is moderate: strong on operational governance in regulated health care and postdeployment monitoring, weaker on conversational LLM-specific governance.

axial_codes: auditable decision-making over system life cycle
coding.theme: Operational governance of patient-facing generative AI media in digital health
coding.subtheme: Risk-and-ethics matrix linking deployment decisions to monitoring and change control

synthesis.main_claim: Patient-facing high-fidelity AI-generated video in digital health requires operational, life-cycle governance embedded in institutional review pathways, not only predeployment checks, and this can be supported by a risk-and-ethics matrix that yields actionable deployment dispositions tied to controls and monitoring.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes a risk-and-ethics matrix plotting residual clinical risk against ethical alignment to produce four dispositions (encourage, permit with oversight, restrict or redesign, prohibit), linked to dossier-based review, minimum controls, measurable postdeployment outcomes, provenance, and change control.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text does not report empirical validation, systematic review methods, or quantitative performance of the matrix; governance discussion for China is described as emerging and distributed; conversational AI/LLM deployment is not the primary technology focus.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational/contextual evidence for operational governance, ethics operationalization, human-in-the-loop review, monitoring triggers, and change control in regulated health-care deployments of generative AI; cite cautiously for conversational LLM governance because the article centers on AI-generated video.
